correlation is not causation, and the disentanglement problem is still open.
correlation-based methods are not a reliable indicator of disentanglement and, therefore, cannot be considered as a proof of concept.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
correlation-based models are not necessarily disentangled models, and that the disentangling power of a model should be evaluated on a dataset that is not correlated with the generative factors.
we have created a set of modified datasets that are designed to make the disentanglement task more difficult for the current state-of-the-art disentangling architectures.
we have created datasets that are easy to generate, yet hard to learn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should be cautious when interpreting the results of disentanglement experiments, as they may not be generalizable to the true causal structure of the data.

the current state of the art in unsupervised dis-entanglement learning may be due to exploiting the convenient correlation structure of the standard datasets rather than discovering the true causal structure.
